pr_body: fix #12192 Support SSH for go get
pr_comments:
Awesome, thank you very much!

The only nits seem to be (in my mind):

1. The config name "USE_GIT_CLONE_URL" seems not related to its meaning? 
    * "ssh" and "http/https" are both valid "git clone url".
    * It might be something like "GO_GET_CLONE_URL_PROTOCOL = ssh/https" (only check "ssh" for ssh, other values for http/https?)
3. The `app.example.ini` and `cheatsheet-....-en.md` needs to be updated accordingly.


Thank you again ~~

I won't necessarily hold back this PR, but the more common way to do this is to handle it in your git config. 
```
[url "ssh://git@domain.tld/"]
    insteadOf = https://domain.tld/
```
While it's perhaps nice for Gitea to be able to do this, it could cause confusion when this doesn't work on other forges that don't have a knob for it.

> ```
> [url "ssh://git@domain.tld/"]
>     insteadOf = https://domain.tld/
> ```

Interesting, I have a variant of this in my gitconfig since a long time for all git hosts I use:

```
[url "git@gitea.com:"]
  insteadof = https://gitea.com/
```

This will force git to use SSH, but despite it, I never had any issues with `go get` which to my knowledge only ever used HTTPS. Could it be that `go get` has a fallback to HTTPS when SSH does not work?

`go get` just uses git under the hood (when git is the vcs specified), so it uses this meta tag to pass to `clone`.
From there you're (more or less) in git land.
The `url insteadOf` trick is pretty good, but there is one limitation: if a site admin deploys Gitea in their internal network, they aren't able to force every developer to do so ..... 🤣

I see, so the current flow is:

- go get to HTTPS, gets HTTPS url, git clone changes HTTPS to SSH and clones

Afterwards with the option flipped:

- go get to HTTPS, gets SSH url, git clone SSH, skipping the requirement for gitconfig

> The `url insteadOf` trick is pretty good, but there is one limitation: if a site admin deploys Gitea in their internal network, they aren't able to force every developer to do so ..... 🤣

That's fair, and again why I'm not necessarily blocking this. In a _personal_ opinion I would rather devs understand how to work with it, as that will work across forges, but I do see the benefit of this in certain cases.

> I see, so the current flow is:
> 
>     * go get to HTTPS -> gets HTTPS url, git clone changes HTTPS to SSH
> 
> 
> Afterwards with the option flipped:
> 
>     * go get to HTTPS -> gets SSH url, git clone SSH, skipping the requirement for config

That is correct, this change more or less simply removes the need for the config if this option is flipped. (Unless for some reason you want to use HTTPS, in which case you need the config swapped)

Take a look at the go get protocol, Go client will try different protocol one by one. So maybe we can put both. That means, both meta will be included so which one is work will be decided by Go client.

Yup, if someone could spend some time on confirming that "putting both SSH/HTTPS links" works, or providing some working examples from other git services, that's much better, and no need to add the new config option.
At least, go get will read multiple metas if I'm not wrong. https://github.com/golang/go/blob/a25688d406f2a4296d39b22a2b10aea7178eddc6/src/cmd/go/internal/vcs/discovery.go#L31

- Gitea version (or commit ref): 1.12.1 built with GNU Make 4.2.1, go1.14.4 : bindata, sqlite, sqlite_unlock_notify  
- Git version: 2.24.3
- Operating system: Arch Linux
- Database (use `[x]`):
  - [ ] PostgreSQL
  - [ ] MySQL
  - [ ] MSSQL
  - [x] SQLite
- Can you reproduce the bug at https://try.gitea.io:
  - [ ] Yes (provide example URL)
  - [ ] No
  - [x] Not relevant
- Log gist:

## Description
We have a private gitea repository containing a go module. When we want to `go get git.company.com/organization/private`, gitea returns only the HTTPS link of the repository, not the SSH one.  
To reproduce, one can simply open a link in the browser: `https://git.company.com/organization/private?go-get=1`  
and examine the returned HTML:  
```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
<meta name="go-import" content="git.company.com/organization/private git https://git.company.com/organization/private.git">
<meta name="go-source" content="git.company.com/organization/private _ https://git.company.com/organization/private/src/branch/master{/dir} https://git.company.com/organization/private/src/branch/master{/dir}/{file}#L{line}">
</head>
<body cz-shortcut-listen="true">
go get git.company.com/organization/private
</body>
</html>
```

Here are the relevant source code locations:
```
templates/base/head.tmpl:	<meta name="go-import" content="{{.GoGetImport}} git {{.CloneLink.HTTPS}}">
modules/context/repo.go:	ctx.PlainText(200, []byte(com.Expand(`<meta name="go-import" content="{GoGetImport} git {CloneLink}">`,
modules/context/context.go:		<meta name="go-import" content="{GoGetImport} git {CloneLink}">
```
One can see in these files/lines that only the HTTPS path is ever returned. We expected that this can be at least configured to either return the SSH or HTTPS one. When disabling HTTPS for the repo, the returned links still stayed the same.
comments: I don't think `go get` support SSH protocol.

It does. We use it in production. The meta tag should look as following:
```html
<meta name="go-import" content="git.company.com/organization/private git ssh://git@git.company.com/organization/private">
```

> When a version control system supports multiple protocols, each is tried in turn when downloading. For example, a Git download tries https://, then git+ssh://. 

https://golang.org/cmd/go/#hdr-Remote_import_paths

Simply because every time we do this we're causing a change of schema - I think we need a generic settings system and I'm opening an issue for that.
